title: Fresh eval units come from pilot repositories with hidden tests
body:
Why: evals/d23/preregistration.md (t-ajp3meg #756): the K vs PB claim needs about 188 units for power 0.8 at +9 pp; D23 has 33 untouched units (power 0.217). The two pilots (TS seo-audit-harness, krn-pilot-py) delivered 5/5 hidden PASS each with lead-written hidden tests, so pilot repositories are the fresh-unit source.
Outcome: a unit format and a builder under evals/ that turns a pilot repository task (base SHA, task text, hidden test file, PB spec) into a replayable unit; at least 20 units committed from the two pilot repositories as the first batch, each verified red on base and green on the reference fix.
Proof: test that every committed unit is red on base and green on its reference (scripted, no paid model runs); npm run fast PASS.

Progress (lane): format evals/units/unit.ts, builder and verifier evals/units/cli.ts, 10 units committed (5 TS seo-audit-harness PRs #78-#82, 5 Python krn-pilot-py PRs #3-#7), every one red on base and green on its reference by 'node evals/units/cli.ts verify --sources .krn/sources'. Only 10 of the 20 exist because the pilots delivered only 10 hidden-tested tasks. More units come from: (1) seo-audit-harness open tracker tasks (tasks/t-m3y2ree.json has no hidden test yet) and the lead-listed candidates in the pilot's research handoff; (2) further upstream humanize issues for krn-pilot-py; (3) a third pilot repository. Each new unit needs a lead-written hidden test before any arm runs, then 'node evals/units/cli.ts build'. Task stays open until 20.
Fable plan 1114c: K delivered 10/10 on the first units, which suggests a ceiling; run the PB arm on the existing units before building many more (deferred: memory quota-before-big-runs).
